dispositions.reason: AC-7 is worded as a process-wide memory guarantee that a unit test cannot show, and the server never stored the secret anyway; the SPEC must re-word it into something testable (e.g. no record, cache or module state holds the secret) before any plan can cover it.
The SPEC does not say whether a deprecated (grace-period) key may manage keys; that is a security-intent decision the SPEC lacks, and the plan cannot choose it without changing stated behaviour.
The plan must either add a guard for revoking the last active admin key or own key, or explicitly list the self-lockout as an accepted limit in Risks (with a test if guarded); today it does neither.
The plan should state in Risks (and README if appropriate) that the 2 to 3 migration is forward-only and the upgrade cannot be rolled back to the previous release, or declare a rollback path.
A SPEC constraint (cross-org key reads 404 not_found on every key route) has no planned test; add a build-owned regression test for rotate and revoke and declare its test file in ## Files.
The no-enumeration claim is stated as fact in the plan; label it advisory and plan a test that a wrong secret for a revoked or expired key id still reads 401 unauthenticated, declaring the test file.
Showing key state in GET /keys or logging deprecated-key use is not in the SPEC scope; the plan states it was deliberately not planned (Risks, Listing keys), so it is an accepted bound.

The five behaviours are implementation choices the plan already lists openly in Risks (Plan decisions not stated in the SPEC) and the README step documents the 409; none contradicts a SPEC criterion, so the build does not need a change.
Minor: the injected clock exists only so the 24 h boundary is reachable in tests; no AC asserts audit timestamps or invoice-handler time, so the partial injection does not affect the build.
